artists.biography: Devo is an American New Wave band formed in 1972 consisting of members from Kent and Akron, Ohio. The classic line-up of the band includes two sets of brothers, the Mothersbaughs (Mark and Bob) and the Casales (Gerald and Bob), along with Alan Myers. The band had a No. 14 Billboard chart hit in 1980 with the single "Whip It", and has maintained a cult following throughout its existence. Their style over time has shifted between punk, art rock, post-punk, and New Wave. Their music and stage show mingle kitsch science fiction themes, deadpan surrealist humor, and mordantly satirical social commentary. Their often discordant pop songs feature unusual synthetic instrumentation and time signatures that have proven influential on subsequent popular music, particularly New Wave, industrial and alternative rock artists. Devo was also a pioneer of the music video, creating many memorable clips for the Laser Disc format, with "Whip It" getting heavy airplay in the early days of MTV.

The collection spans key tracks from all nine of Devo's studio albums, alongside rarities, B-sides, demos, and alternate versions, showcasing their distinctive synth-driven sound characterized by concise, punchy compositions and a fusion of primal energy with sophisticated electronic textures. The album highlights Devo's evolution in style while maintaining their signature blend of quirky, experimental synth-pop and rock elements.

This release holds a significant place in Devo's discography as a definitive retrospective, celebrating their legacy from their formation in 1973 through 2023. It offers both longtime fans and new listeners an extensive overview of the band's creative output, including multiple versions of classics like "Mongoloid" and "Jocko Homo," illustrating the band's innovative approach to their material. Critically, the box set has been well received, praised for its meticulous curation and sound quality, earning high ratings and being described as indispensable for Devo enthusiasts. Commercially, it serves as a testament to Devo's enduring influence in the electronic and rock genres, reaffirming their status as experimental pop pioneers.
